title: Teaching the Plan of Salvation (Part 2)
focus: Practice topic: the Atonement of Jesus Christ
intro: The Atonement of Jesus Christ is the center of the plan of salvation. In this lesson learners study how the Savior overcomes the effects of the Fall, feel His love, and practise teaching the whole plan with a simple diagram.
preparation: Study Isaiah 53:3–5; 1 Corinthians 15:20–22; Alma 7:11–13; Alma 11:42–44; Alma 34:8–9; and Doctrine and Covenants 19:15–19. Be ready to show a short video on God’s love for the world. Pray for each learner by name.

sections.title: The Atonement
paras: Ask learners to read John 3:16 in silence and think how this one verse sums up the plan of salvation. Let a few share. Ask each learner to say, in one sentence, why the Savior’s sacrifice is needed.

Name the effects of the Fall that touch everyone: physical death, sin and spiritual death, and suffering and sorrow. Write the three on the board with these scriptures: 1 Corinthians 15:20–22 and Alma 11:42–44 for physical death; Alma 34:8–9 and Doctrine and Covenants 19:15–19 for sin; Isaiah 53:3–5 and Alma 7:11–13 for suffering. Divide the class into three groups, one for each. Each group studies its passages and explains to the class how the Savior overcomes that effect.

sections.title: Feeling the truth
paras: Show the video about God’s love for the world. Ask learners to look for ways Jesus Christ showed His love. Then ask what moved them, and how that love could shape the way they serve.

Invite the Spirit by sharing your testimony. Ask why missionaries should often testify of Jesus Christ. One role of the Holy Ghost is to testify of the Savior (see John 15:26; 3 Nephi 11:32). President Boyd K. Packer taught the same idea in “The Candle of the Lord,” Ensign, January 1983: a testimony grows as we bear it.

sections.title: The plan of salvation in one picture
paras: Let learners study the plan of salvation diagram and draw their own version. They study one section at a time and write what an investigator needs to know in each part.

Ask: What impact will our choices here have after we die? How does the Judgment shape our choices now? How does the Atonement touch our life before earth, here and after death? Ask why we should explain these truths in a simple, clear way.

sections.title: Teaching in pairs
paras: Explain that families are part of God’s plan and continue beyond death, which is one of the great doctrines of the Restoration. Pairs prepare to teach someone the plan of salvation using the chart they made or the diagram. Stress that they should speak in their own words.
After each pair teaches, ask what went well and what could improve. Close with testimony.

steps.why: Teach the idea and why it matters for a missionary.

examples.title: Name the three effects of the Fall
examples.text: Write physical death, sin and suffering on the board. Use one verse for each and show how the Atonement answers them.

examples.title: Show the Savior’s love
examples.text: Read John 3:16 and Alma 7:11–13. Explain why the Savior suffered and what that means for each person.

examples.title: Draw the plan on one page
examples.text: Draw before earth, mortality, the Judgment and kingdoms of glory. Show where the Atonement fits.

steps.why: Show one example of what learners will do.

examples.title: Teach the Atonement in three minutes
examples.text: Say what the Fall did, what the Savior did and what we do in response. Read one verse and testify.

examples.title: Teach to someone who feels unworthy
examples.text: Show how to share Alma 7:11–13 with someone who feels alone in their pain.

examples.title: Teach the plan with a diagram
examples.text: Draw the plan while you explain, and ask one question after each part.

steps.why: Learners practise in pairs or small groups.

examples.title: Teach in pairs
examples.text: Each pair teaches a six-minute lesson on the Atonement with a diagram, one verse and a testimony.

examples.title: Answer a question
examples.text: A friend asks, “Why do we need a Savior?” Answer with the Fall and a verse.

examples.title: Draw it from memory
examples.text: Each learner draws the plan on a clean page and explains it to a partner.

steps.why: Name what went well and what can improve.

examples.title: Partner feedback
examples.text: The learner who was taught says what was clearest and what felt most sincere. The teacher writes one thing to keep and one to improve.

examples.title: Three questions
examples.text: Ask: What went well? What would you change? What helped the listener most to understand the Atonement? Begin with the good.

examples.title: Simple checklist
examples.text: Was it simple? Was a scripture used and explained? Was the listener invited to act? Did the teacher speak with sincerity?

steps.why: Practise again with what was learned.

examples.title: Switch roles
examples.text: The learner who listened now teaches. Leave time for feedback both ways, then ask a few to share what they learned.

examples.title: Improve one thing
examples.text: Each learner teaches again and changes one thing from the feedback: a clearer sentence, a better scripture or a warmer invitation.

examples.title: Teach a new partner
examples.text: Find a new partner. Teach the same lesson again in a few minutes. Share one insight with the class.

testimony: Testify of the Savior’s love and of the peace the Atonement brings. Invite learners to share what the Atonement means to them.

tips.text: Let learners study different passages, then share what they found.
Give learners time to feel a truth, not just understand it.
Ask learners to bear testimony often.
Use a simple drawing to explain a big idea.

quote.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

study: Read Alma 7:11–13 together and ask what the Savior took upon Himself and why.
invitations: Practise drawing the plan of salvation diagram and explaining it in your own words.
Think of someone who is struggling. Write how the Atonement could bless them.
Study a recent conference talk about the Atonement and write one thing it teaches you.
Pray for a chance to share the plan of salvation with someone.

blocks.text: Welcome the class warmly. Begin with a prayer and a short thought from scripture to invite the Holy Ghost.
What happened when you tried last lesson’s invitation? Who would like to share?
Listen for: real experiences, effort made, one thing learned.
Try saying: “Before we start, who would like to tell us what happened when they tried last week’s invitation?”
